english.title: Arrest for Examination by an Immigration Officer
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) having been arrested by a constable for

(A)_[being a person who may be required to submit to examination under paragraph 2 of Schedule 2 to the Immigration Act 1971]_
(B)_[being a person whose leave to enter has been suspended under paragraph 2A of Schedule 2 to the Immigration Act 1971]_
(C)_[being a person who has been required to submit to further examination under paragraph 3(1A) of Schedule 2 to the Immigration Act 1971]_
(D)_[being a person in respect of whom direction may be given under any of paragraphs 8 to 10A or 12 to 14 of Schedule 2 to the Immigration Act 1971]_

are detained pending examination and pending a decision to give or refuse leave to enter In accordance with paragraphs 16 and 17 of Schedule 2 to the Immigration Act 1971
english.legislation: Pursuant to paragraph 17 of Schedule 2 to the Immigration Act 1971.

english.notes:
The above 'wording' is not an offence.

(i) This wording is supplied by PNLD for information only (some forces do prepare a 'charge form' for administrative purposes.(ii) Suggested wording to be used when exercising this power of arrest:

“ I am arresting you on suspicion that you are a person liable to immigration detention. This is because I suspect you [give reason outlined in paragraph 16 of Schedule 2 to the Immigration Act 1971”, “have ....” This is not an arrest for a criminal offence. Do you understand?”

(i) A person shall be deemed to be in legal custody at any time when he is detained following this arrest. Following the arrest, the individual should into custody and the Immigration Enforcement (IE) National Command and Control Unit contacted to arrange collection of the individual for further dealing. This is a non-PACE matter.
(ii) Any person detained following arrest may be taken in the custody of a constable, an immigration officer, or any person acting under the authority of an immigration officer, to and from any place where his attendance is required for the purpose of ascertaining his citizenship or nationality or of making arrangements for his admission to a country or territory other than the United Kingdom, or where he is required to be for any other purpose connected with the operation of this Act (paragraph 18(3) of Schedule 2).(iii) Places of detention following an arrest are listed in the Immigration (Places of Detention) Direction 2014 (No.2).(iv) Where a person is detained or liable to be detained under paragraph 16, any immigration officer, constable or prison officer, or any other person authorised by the Secretary of State, may take all such steps as may be reasonably necessary for photographing, measuring or otherwise identifying him (paragraph 18(2 of Schedule 2)).
(v) Where a criminal offence is suspected, the administrative power of arrest under schedule 2 and in this document would not be the correct power of arrest to apply in those circumstances. Instead, officers should use their PACE powers of arrest.

other.powersofarrest: Paragraph 17 of Schedule 2 to the Immigration Act 1971 provides a power of arrest for a constable who has used where the officer has reasonable suspicion the individual is liable to be held in immigration detention for one of the reasons specified in paragraph 16 of Schedule 2.
